column3: The Hebrew says they will “know” the land, rather than “enjoy it.”
The Hebrew explicitly names their carcasses.
The Hebrew retains bearing their whoredom and describes their carcasses coming to an end in the wilderness.
The Hebrew repeats the correspondence of a day to a year.
The Hebrew says the men died by the plague, rather than expressing this as being struck down.
The Hebrew does not separately add “only.”
The Hebrew says “Here we are” and gives their sin as a reason with “for,” rather than preceding their resolve with “but.”
The Hebrew retains the LORD’s “mouth” rather than simply His commandment.
The Hebrew says they may be defeated “before” their enemies, rather than “by” them.
The Hebrew gives the peoples singular collective names.
The Hebrew mentions the ark before Moses and specifies the midst of the camp.
